Wanzhou|China.f: About 47 percent of Wanzhou's old urban area was submerged and had to be relocated because of the Three Gorges Dam.

Shihezi|China.f: Shihezi began in 1951 when General Wang Zhen chose the site for a new People's Liberation Army base.

Tacheng|China.f: About 58,000 ethnic Kazakhs left Tacheng for the Soviet Union in spring 1962, an exodus known as the Yi-Ta incident.

Libo|China.f: Two sites in Libo County, Xiaoqikong and Dongduo, are part of the South China Karst, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.

Ulanhot|China.f: Ulanhot was the first capital of Inner Mongolia, China's first autonomous region, from 1 May 1947 until 1949.

Hejing|China.f: Hejing County borders 15 other cities and counties, said to be more than any other county in the world.

Qitai|China.f: Qitai County sits on an estimated 280.8 billion tonnes of coal, the largest reserves of any county in China.

Longzi|China.f: Lhunze means self-existing pinnacle in Tibetan, and the 14th Dalai Lama stopped here in March 1959 while fleeing to India.
